title: A Custom Multiphoton Microscopy Platform for Live Imaging of Mouse Cornea and Conjunctiva
protocol: Build a system based on an upright microscope with water immersion 20x 1.00 NA objective.
Use Ti: Sapphire laser as the excitation source.
Set the laser output wavelength at 880 nm for EGFP and 940 nm for tdTomato.
Include two dichroic mirrors (495 nm and 580 nm) for the separation of SHG/EGFP and EGFP/tdTomato.
Spectrally separate the SHG signals, EGFP and tdTomato by bandpass filters 434/17nm, 510/84nm and 585/40nm.
Set the laser power to be about 35 mW for imaging cornea and 50 mW for limbus.
Measure the laser power before the laser passes the optical system.
Use 8-12-week-old mice for the experiment.
Intramuscularly inject 50-80 mg/kg of tiletamine HCl and zolazepam HCl for general anesthesia.
Check for the lack of response to withdrawal reflex by pinching a toe.
Place the mouse under anesthesia on a heated stage.
Insert the temperature monitoring probe into the anus fully.
Use a custom-designed stereotaxic mouse holder for live imaging of ocular surface.
Insert ear bars into the external auditory meatus and maintain head stability.
Topically apply 0.4% oxybuprocaine hydrochloride solution in saline to anesthetize the ocular surface.
Wait 3 min after applying the anesthetic solution before proceeding with imaging.
Protrude the eyeball by manual eyelid retraction carefully.
Place a loop of polyethylene tube along the eyelid margin to expose the ocular surface.
Stabilize the eyeball with a No. 5 Dumont forceps covered in a loop of polyethylene tube.
Screw the forceps using a knob on the distal part of the eye holder to maintain stability.
Apply an eye gel with a refractive index of 1.338 on the corneal surface as an immersion medium to maintain moisture every hour.
Rotate the eyeball using a holder attached to a stepper-motorized stage for imaging across the entire corneal surface from central to peripheral regions.
Supplement eye gel every hour to prevent clouding in the cornea during imaging and ensure image quality.
Set the first and last slide in every stack to reduce dropping motion artifacts.
Turn on the microscope software using the symbol provided in the interface.
Select appropriate PMT gain and digital gain to visualize cellular structures in the ocular surface.
Enter numerical values for image resolution and z-step, such as 512 x 512 and 1 μm respectively.
Click the Start button to collect z-serial images.
Acquire live images twice in the same area: first at 880 nm excitation for SHG/EGFP signals collection, second at 940 nm excitation for EGFP/tdTomato signals collection.
Load z-serial images into Fiji software.
Select the plugin Median 3D filter in Fiji to reduce background noises.
Select the Package Unsharp Mask filter in Fiji to sharpen the images.
Click “Auto” in brightness/contrast to automatically optimize the quality of images.
Save the images as image sequences to be able to export the z-serial images.
Load z-serial images into commercial software for 3D reconstruction using volume rendering.
